tags.name: wire
tags.description: Wire.js reactive element. Its own content is a template: `{{ expr }}` writes an escaped result, `{{{ expr }}}` writes unescaped markup. Re-renders only for the signals named in `to`, `for`, `if` and `with`. Always close it, `<wire />` is not valid HTML. Cannot carry `on:`, `:` or `bind:` attributes.

attributes.name: to
attributes.description: Write a signal's value into the element as escaped text. Takes a signal (`@name`) only. Cannot be used if the element has content; mutually exclusive with `for`.

attributes.name: with
attributes.description: Re-render the element's template whenever any of these signals changes. One or more signals separated by spaces (`@a @b`). List every signal the template reads, or it goes stale.

attributes.name: for
attributes.description: Render the element's content once per item of an array. Takes a signal (`@name`) or an expression (`@{ expr }`). Mutually exclusive with `to`. Loop variables are in scope for nested elements.

attributes.name: each
attributes.description: Name of the variable that holds the current item inside a `for`. Literal only, must be a valid JavaScript variable name; requires `for`.

attributes.name: if
attributes.description: Only render while truthy, otherwise the element is emptied and hidden. Takes a signal (`@name`) or an expression (`@{ expr }`). An expression only re-evaluates for the signals named in the element's attributes.

attributes.name: else
attributes.description: Render when the directly preceding `<wire>` sibling's `if` (or `else`) was false. May carry its own `if` to chain (`else if`). Flag attribute.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: A plain attribute, never parsed as Wire syntax. `class`, `style`, `title`, `data-*` and `aria-*` are plain attributes too; any other attribute throws.

attributes.name: class
attributes.description: CSS classes. A plain attribute, never parsed as Wire syntax.

attributes.name: style
attributes.description: Inline style. A plain attribute, never parsed as Wire syntax.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: A plain attribute, never parsed as Wire syntax.

tags.name: component
tags.description: Wire.js component. Without `instance` it defines a template (declared args via `arg:name`); with `instance` it renders that template. A component template sees only its own args, signals and globals. Always close it. Cannot carry `on:`, `:` or `bind:` attributes.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Component name. Required. Used to register a template, or to select which template an instance renders. Names are global and unique.

attributes.name: instance
attributes.description: Marks this element as an instance of the named component instead of a template definition. Flag attribute.

attributes.name: arg:
attributes.description: Component argument, written `arg:<name>`. HTML lowercases attribute names, so write multi-word names in kebab-case: `arg:unit-label` is `unitLabel` in the template. On a template definition it is a bare flag declaring an argument; on an instance it takes a literal (always a string), a signal (`@name`, reactive) or an expression (`@{ expr }`, typed, evaluated when the instance renders). Arguments left out are `null`, undeclared ones throw.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: A plain attribute, never parsed as Wire syntax.

attributes.name: class
attributes.description: CSS classes. A plain attribute, never parsed as Wire syntax.

attributes.name: style
attributes.description: Inline style. A plain attribute, never parsed as Wire syntax.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: A plain attribute, never parsed as Wire syntax.

globalAttributes.name: with
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js: signals (`@a @b`) that a bound element's `:name="@{ expr }"` expressions read. The expressions are re-evaluated when any of them changes.

globalAttributes.name: on:click
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js event: run `@{ code }` when the event fires. The code is statements with the loop variables, signals and `event` in scope.

globalAttributes.name: on:input
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js event: run `@{ code }` on each input. The code is statements with the loop variables, signals and `event` in scope.

globalAttributes.name: on:change
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js event: run `@{ code }` when the value is committed. The code is statements with the loop variables, signals and `event` in scope.

globalAttributes.name: on:submit
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js event: run `@{ code }` on submit. Call `event.preventDefault()` yourself to stop the page navigating.

globalAttributes.name: on:keydown
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js event: run `@{ code }` on key down, for example `@{ if (event.key === 'Enter') add() }`.

globalAttributes.name: on:keyup
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js event: run `@{ code }` on key up.

globalAttributes.name: on:mousedown
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js event: run `@{ code }` on press. Use it for rows that re-render often, since a click is lost if its element is replaced before release.

globalAttributes.name: on:focus
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js event: run `@{ code }` when the element gains focus.

globalAttributes.name: on:blur
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js event: run `@{ code }` when the element loses focus.

globalAttributes.name: bind:value
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js two-way binding: the field shows the signal and typing sets it. Takes a State (`@name`). `number` and `range` inputs give numbers. For `<select>` it listens to `change`.

globalAttributes.name: bind:checked
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js two-way binding: a checkbox's checked state and a State (`@name`) as a boolean. For radios use `:checked` with `on:change`.

globalAttributes.name: :class
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: adds and removes only its own class names, so static classes stay. Takes a signal (`@name`) or an expression (`@{ expr }` with `with`).

globalAttributes.name: :style
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: replaces the whole `style` attribute. Takes a signal (`@name`) or an expression (`@{ expr }` with `with`).

globalAttributes.name: :disabled
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: `true` sets the attribute, `false`, `null` or `undefined` removes it.

globalAttributes.name: :hidden
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: `true` sets the attribute, `false`, `null` or `undefined` removes it.

globalAttributes.name: :checked
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: written as the `checked` property.

globalAttributes.name: :selected
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: written as the `selected` property.

globalAttributes.name: :value
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: written as the `value` property, and left alone if the field already shows it.

globalAttributes.name: :href
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: sets the attribute from a signal or expression, and removes it for `false`, `null` or `undefined`.

globalAttributes.name: :src
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: sets the attribute from a signal or expression, and removes it for `false`, `null` or `undefined`.

globalAttributes.name: :title
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: sets the attribute from a signal or expression, and removes it for `false`, `null` or `undefined`.

globalAttributes.name: :placeholder
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: sets the attribute from a signal or expression, and removes it for `false`, `null` or `undefined`.

globalAttributes.name: :min
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: sets the attribute from a signal or expression, for example a range limited by another signal.

globalAttributes.name: :max
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: sets the attribute from a signal or expression, for example a range limited by another signal.

globalAttributes.name: :aria-label
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: sets the attribute from a signal or expression. To write the text `false` use `@{ String(x) }`.

globalAttributes.name: :aria-expanded
globalAttributes.description: Wire.js binding: `false` removes the attribute, so write `@{ String(open.get()) }` to keep the text `false`.
